claim.summary: Fix a binary monic d(z) of degree b>=0 and nu>=b. Given a shared binary division-free unbounded-fanin circuit, gate/wire size S and depth delta, for the COMPLETE coefficient list a0(y),...,a_nu(y) of g=sum a_i z^i, with d|g in F2[y,z], h=g/d has circuit size O(S+(nu+1)^2), depth<=delta+3. Put u=nu-b,d*=t^b d(1/t), and let c_l be the t^l coefficient of 1/d* for l<=u, fixed binary constants; h_j=sum_(l<=u-j)c_l a_(b+j+l), reconstruct h=sum h_j z^j using ordinary power wires. Nonzero g has actual joint degree deg h=deg g-b. Fixed nonuniform divisor and degree parameters, not variable inputs. No coefficient access from an implicit g circuit, PC-degree transfer, proof-image inclusion, binary general quotient algorithm or Frege advance is supplied.

Gate weights use maximum at sums and sum at products, with sum inputs scaled by nonnegative powers of B. If F generates the unit ideal and includes B, and H has common polynomial value h on every formal Hilbert-like coefficient certificate, the rational-pivot identity gives g=B^k h regardless of placeholder degree. This is a dividend construction only; no binary bounded-depth circuit for the quotient h is obtained.

claim.summary: There is no generic polynomial-size fixed-depth operation extracting arbitrary homogeneous components from all polynomial-size fixed-depth binary arithmetic circuits of polynomial degree. Already G_n=product(1+x_i), q=2^a, n=2q-1 has degree-q component e_q evaluating to majority, since binomial(w,q) mod2 is the a-th bit of w. Such an operation would contradict Smolensky's majority lower bound for AC0[2]. Binary constants and unbounded-fanin gates with wire size are essential.
claim.assessment: Working attributed elementary consequence of the published majority lower bound, medium reviewed. Does not rule out special component extraction with additional hypotheses or large-field interpolation.
